A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Graph (Graph Theory)|graph]] and $k \in \Z_{>0}$.
Then $G$ has an [[Definition:Independent Set (Graph Theory)|independent set]] of size $k$ {{iff}} the [[Definition:Complement of Graph|complement]] $\overline G$ has a [[Definition:Clique (Graph Theory)|clique]] of size $k$.

B_source.statement: The [[Definition:Clique Problem|clique problem]] asks whether a graph $H$ contains $k$ mutually [[Definition:Adjacent Vertices|adjacent]] vertices.

derived.k mutually adjacent vertices in H: k mutually non-adjacent vertices in G

object_map.reformulation: Complement the graph: replace G by G-bar, so non-edges become edges.

validity_conditions: A set is independent in G iff it is a clique in the complement G-bar, because adjacency is exactly inverted by complementation.
The complement is computable in polynomial time, so this is a valid (poly-time) reduction preserving the answer.
proof_plan: Given $\tuple {G, k}$, construct the [[Definition:Complement of Graph|complement graph]] $\overline G$ on the same vertex set, with $u v$ an edge of $\overline G$ {{iff}} $u v$ is not an edge of $G$.
A set $S$ is [[Definition:Independent Set (Graph Theory)|independent]] in $G$ {{iff}} no two vertices of $S$ are adjacent in $G$, {{iff}} every two are adjacent in $\overline G$.
Query the clique problem for $\tuple {\overline G, k}$.
